prediction_text: Direction: Hillary Clinton wins the 2016 US presidential election (the conference panel consensus call). Specifics: the Democrat defeats Donald Trump on 8 November 2016, in line with the polling lead recorded on the card and with the majority judgement of the forecasting panel convened at the Costa Mesa conference; the win is read as the establishment/continuity candidate prevailing over the insurgent. Timing: single-date event, 8 November 2016 (day-scale per the question). Confidence is only mid-range: the card supplies no charts for either candidate, and panel consensus plus polls are the stated basis — the prediction is recorded as the panel's collective call, not as a chart-derived certainty.
basis:
tradition/system: not labelled on the input card; system actually used: Western mundane/electional astrology (panel consensus reading).
Basis: card-given facts — Clinton v Trump, most polls favouring Clinton, an international astrology conference election panel sitting in October 2016. This case is the panel-as-a-whole: its collective judgement is the object of the prediction, and it aligns with the polling facts on the card. The one panellist singled out in the companion case WP-005 is treated there separately; here no individual dissent is imported. No natal/ingress charts are on the card, so confidence is capped.
